OFFICIAL CANVASS OF THE APRIL 10, 2018 GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION
Presenter: City Clerk, Britt Avrit
Recommendation:
Adopt Resolution No. 18-10, reciting the facts of the General Municipal Election held on Tuesday, April 10, 2018, declaring the results and such other matters as provided by law regarding the election of two Council Members.
Election Code Sections 10262, 10263 and 10264 require, among other things, the City Clerk to declare to the legislative body the results of the General Municipal Election. The City Clerk published the Notice of Election, which was given in time, form and manner as prescribed by law. The voting precincts were properly established, and election officers appointed. In all respects, the election was held and conducted, votes were cast, received and canvassed, and returns made and declared in time, form and manner as required by the provisions of the Elections Code of the State of California.

City Council Recommendation:
Approve Amendment 2 to professional services agreement with California Choice Energy Authority ("CCEA") for support provided by city staff and regulatory services for all CCEA administrative service agreements; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to approve amendments up to 10% annually.

Approve Amendment 2 to professional services agreement with the City of Lancaster ("the City") for support provided by city staff and regulatory services for all CCEA administrative support agreements; and authorize the Executive Director, or his designee, to approve amendments up to 10% annually.

Approve a professional services agreement with Pavement Engineering, Inc., of Santa Clarita, California, in the amount of $324,465.00 (including Optional Task 11), with a 10% contingency, for citywide pavement evaluation and analysis, and authorize the City Manager or his designee to sign all documents. The consultant selection process was made in accordance with Government Code 4526 and 53060.
As part of the of the professional services agreement, the Consultant will inspect approximately 343 centerline miles of streets and alleyways, which accounts for approximately 75% of the cityâ€™s entire road network. The Consultant will also update the Pavement Condition Index (PCI) ratings for Lancaster. PCI is the metric commonly used by agencies to rate the condition of a road or alleyway.

Award contract to Stantec Consulting Ltd. of Lancaster, California, for Task Order No. 23 in accordance with the 2016-2018 Multi-Year Professional Services Agreement in the amount of $499,718.00, authorize contingency in the amount of $49,971.80, for a total contract amount not-to-exceed $549,689.80, and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to sign all documents. The contract will cover Engineering Design (Plans, Specifications and Estimates, PS&Eâ€™s) and Environmental Services under Service Group Category 1 for Roadway and Structures Engineering for Public Works Construction Project (PWCP) 17-005 â€“ 2020 SRTS Pedestrian Improvements.
The project will construct over 6,200 lineal feet of new sidewalk, 1,000 lineal feet of sidewalk widening, 12,500 lineal feet of bike lanes, 88 bulb-outs, over 230 curb ramps, crosswalks, street lighting, pavement repairs, speed humps, bike racks, various utility improvements, driveway modifications, removal and installation of 125 trees, irrigation installation and repairs, drainage improvements and signing, striping and markings.

CC 6. Reject all bids for Public Works Construction Project No. 18-005, Maintenance Yard Recycling Center Improvements. Two of the three bids received were determined to be non-responsive, and all bids significantly exceeded the project budget.
This project was designed with AC pavement drive aisle, impermeable slab with containment curb and containment bays for collection at the Recycling Center. On January 18, 2018, at 11:00 a.m., the City conducted a bid opening for Public Works Construction Project No. 18-005. Three (3) sealed bid envelopes were received, opened, and read aloud.

CC 7. Designate the City Manager as the signatory representing the City (in its capacity as a property owner) on documents related to the renewal of the Downtown Lancaster Property-Based Improvement District (PBID) for the 2018 and all future renewals of the PBID; and authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute related documents, as and to the extent authorized by the City Council.
As the City is a property owner in downtown Lancaster, this item authorizes the City Manager to act as signatory on behalf of the City (as a property owner) during the petition drive phase of the PBID formation process. The present action does not obligate the City to participate in the PBID assessment.
CC7
CC 8. Enter into a five-year lease purchase agreement with GM Financial (Antelope Valley Chevrolet) to replace seven (7) light duty fleet vehicles in FY 17-18.
Staff performed an analysis of the overall state of the Cityâ€™s light duty fleet. The analysis included an evaluation of our current fleet, the identification of the vehicles in most critical need of replacement, and a review of the fleet purchase/financing options available to the City. Eight vehicles were identified as being in most need of replacement due to their high repair costs, mileage and poor overall functioning. These eight vehicles were seven trucks, which we will continue purchasing standard trucks as replacements; and one car for replacement with an electric vehicle.
CC8
CC 9. Adopt Resolution No. 18-11, adopting a list of projects for fiscal year 2018-2019 funded by Senate Bill 1 (SB 1), the Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017.
SB 1 emphasizes the importance of accountability and transparency; therefore, in order to be eligible for RMRA funding, statute requires cities to adopt a proposed project list at a regular public meeting. The list of proposed projects must include a description and location of each proposed project, a proposed schedule for the projectâ€™s completion, and the estimated useful life of the improvement. Cities must also adopt RMRA funded projects into a cityâ€™s operating or capital improvement budget. Cities must then submit the completed SB 1 Proposed Project List form to the California Transportation Commission (CTC), in order to receive its apportionment of RMRA funds from the State Controller by May 1st of each year.

The proposed action would allow for the transfer of security to BYDâ€™s expansion site at 50th Street West and Avenue H in order to facilitate BYDâ€™s efforts to secure financing needed for their continuing growth. This site encompasses APNs 3269-011-015 and 3269-011-007. The underlying commitments to install public improvements will remain the same; the new site is simply being substituted for the current one as security.

NEW BUSINESS
CCEA NB 1.
Adopt Resolution No. CCEA 01-18, approving and authorizing the City of Pico Rivera and the City of Rancho Mirage to enter into the Joint Exercise Powers Agreement for the California Choice Energy Authority.
On April 11, 2017, the City of Pico Rivera, a newly formed CCA, approved a Resolution to join the Authority for the purpose of receiving operational and administrative support services from the Authority, including the purchase and sale of electricity, technical support, and data management services, on behalf of their CCA. Pico Rivera's CCA program, Pico Rivera Innovative Municipal Energy ("PRIME") will be completely operational in May 2018. On October 19, 2017, the City of Rancho Mirage, a newly formed CCA, approved a Resolution to join the Authority for the purpose of receiving operational and administrative support services from the Authority, including the purchase and sale of electricity, technical support, and data management services, on behalf of their CCA. Rancho Mirage's CCA program, Rancho Mirage Energy Authority ("RMEA") will launch in May 2018.
CCEA NB1
CCEA NB1 attachment
NB 1. Hotel Stimulus Program
Recommendation:
Introduce Ordinance No. 1042, adding chapter 3.37 to the Lancaster Municipal Code establishing a Hotel Stimulus Program; and authorizing the City Manager or his designee to execute all related documents.
Staff proposes the creation of a Hotel Stimulus Program (HSP) to incentivize the construction of hotels designed to create maximum value for the community. In exchange for the incentives, the participating hotels will agree to operate at the proposed level of service and brand for a minimum of 11 years. The proposed Hotel Stimulus Program holds the potential to generate substantial revenue to the City in the form of both TOT and property tax for decades to come, as well as create new jobs for members of our local community. In addition, it will help provide much-needed accommodations for local industry, thus attracting an increased number of visitors who will in turn further boost the Lancaster economy. Finally, with the elimination of redevelopment in California, staff believes that the proposed HSP will provide a prudent level of incentives to attract high quality hotels and additional hospitality industry jobs to Lancaster.
